phases.name: Core product & macOS
phases.desc: SRS engine, entitlement, specialty-pack architecture complete. The macOS app is signed, notarized, and now publicly released — v0.1.0-beta.2 is a live, downloadable pre-release (macOS + Linux AppImage builds, working auto-update manifest). This closed a real gap found this week: the build had been notarized and ready since July 29 but sitting undistributed.

phases.name: Full curriculum, A1–B2
phases.desc: 126 units, 30,609 cards. Every level has shipped at target density and passed at least one adversarial content-quality audit.

phases.name: Windows & Linux desktop
phases.desc: OS-event hooks and packaging are code-complete on both platforms. Blocked on Windows code-signing setup and on real-hardware verification — see Blockers.

phases.name: Cloud sync & auth
phases.desc: Done and live-verified end to end on the packaged Mac app, not just in a development server. A real account holder signed in via Apple through the actual desktop build, recorded reviews on two independent devices at once, and both were confirmed as separate entries in the production database with correct automatic conflict handling — no review ever silently overwritten or lost, by design. The final verification pass caught and closed out two real, live-reachable issues before they could reach a broader release (a stale local packaging step, and a sign-in edge case specific to the desktop app), both fixed and covered by new automated tests same day. A follow-on improvement also cut typical cross-device sync latency from minutes to seconds. This unblocks push notifications, the last piece before mobile development begins.

phases.name: Mobile — iOS & Android
phases.desc: Not started. Queued behind sync backend; will ship from the same codebase via Tauri's mobile target, not a separate native rewrite.

phaseMethodology: the 86% headline weights each phase by its share of remaining engineering scope to a full five-platform, synced release (Core 35% · Content 25% · Windows/Linux 15% · Sync 15% · Mobile 10%), not by how many tickets are closed. A raw ticket count would read materially higher and overstate where things stand — mobile in particular is still fully ahead.

content.note: Every level has shipped its full unit plan and cleared this project's mechanical quality gate (no unit missing a tier, no duplicate sentences, hints present). B1 sits furthest from its stretch card-count target — the tradeoff made there was breadth of grammar coverage over raw card volume; it does not affect the level's completeness or its audit status below.

blockers.title: Windows code-signing setup
blockers.desc: Release pipeline and signing code are written. Needs an Azure Trusted Signing account, identity verification, and six credentials supplied once, then Windows builds sign automatically going forward.

blockers.title: Windows / Linux hardware verification
blockers.desc: OS-level wake, unlock, and idle-detection hooks are written and compile clean, but have only been checked on macOS. Needs real Windows and Linux machines (or CI runners) for final manual verification.
